A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CB-SAE research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated sections and renumbered tables.

before.justification: v1 reports original SAE and CB-SAE evaluations using LLaVA-1.5, LLaVA-MORE and UnCLIP, alongside ablations, sensitivity analyses and qualitative results.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds SAE-architecture comparisons, a CB-AE ablation, threshold and reconstruction analyses, and cross-task correlation results.

M1.justification: The pruning rule, retained frozen SAE, concept bottleneck, concept selection and three training objectives remain unchanged. The additional SAE variants and removal of the SAE component are evaluation settings and ablations, not revisions to the proposed procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions retain ImageNet-1K, the same concept-set coverage studies, and LLaVA text-generation and UnCLIP image-generation tasks. The new analyses use existing coverage; the 1329 shared concepts form a matched analysis subset.

E2.justification: Beyond v1's Matryoshka SAE comparisons, v2 Tables 3-4 evaluate Top-k SAE, Batch Top-k SAE and a standalone CB-AE without the SAE component. This substantially broadens the evaluated alternatives to include other SAE architectures and a concept-only comparator.

E3.justification: Existing training and steering protocols remain unchanged. Added diagnostic protocols include a native-CLIP steering threshold of 0.173 alongside the original SAE-mean threshold of 0.232, individual neuron-zeroing controls, dead-neuron counting and a matched comparison across 1329 concepts.

E4.justification: Appendix C adds investigations of threshold sensitivity, reconstruction contributions of the four neuron groups, robustness across SAE architectures, the contribution of retaining an SAE, and cross-task steerability correlation. These substantially expand the validation beyond v1's retained pruning, loss, sparsity and evaluator-sensitivity analyses.

E5.justification: Appendix C.3 newly reports a p-value of 0.035 for the Pearson correlation between LLaVA and UnCLIP steerability. This adds significance reporting; no additional repeated-run counts, seed variation or confidence intervals are documented.

E6.justification: Original scores are retained, including v1 Tables 3-4 as v2 Tables 5-6. Substantial new findings include architecture-specific scores and dead-neuron counts; CB-AE versus CB-SAE interpretability of 0.308 versus 0.244 and unit-vector steerability of 0.238 versus 0.261; reconstruction-loss changes; and cross-task correlation of 0.06. The alternative threshold yields 29.14% high-interpretability/high-steerability neurons versus 18.84% under the original threshold, not a same-setting performance improvement.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, pruning-set construction, SAE/CB-SAE equations and cosine-cubed loss formula are retained. No new theorem, proof or substantive derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central contribution: combining SAE discovery with user-specified concept control through pruning and a concept bottleneck. The headline interpretability and steerability improvements of 32.1% and 14.5% are unchanged.

C2.justification: New interpretations connect low interpretability with larger reconstruction contributions, explain the CB-AE/CB-SAE tradeoff and characterize steerability as downstream-task/model dependent. Appendix A suggests feature splitting as a possible explanation for incomplete concept coverage. The existing CLIP-Dissect reliability limitation is relocated, not newly introduced.

D1.justification: v2 adds an explicit code repository link on page 1, whereas v1 only promises release. The documented training budget, hyperparameters and hardware remain unchanged; the PDFs do not establish the repository's contents or availability of model weights.

R1.justification: v2 expands citations and explicitly distinguishes its approach from DN-CBM and SpLiCE, while adding feature-splitting and SAE-utility context. The LLaVA-Phi citation is removed. The overall positioning remains unchanged, and the AlignSAE comparison was already present in v1.

P1.justification: The introduction and conclusion are tightened, acknowledgements are expanded, and existing limitations move into a dedicated Appendix A. Original appendix sections A-B become B-C. Most technical prose and the main narrative structure are preserved.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 3-4 and renumbers the existing appendix tables as 5-6. Figures 2-4 receive clearer steering annotations, quadrant percentages and an explicit final inference diagram; Figure 8 labels are refined. These are localized display revisions within the retained document layout.

improvement.justification: The added architecture comparisons, CB-AE ablation and threshold control strengthen empirical support beyond v1 and clarify the method's component tradeoffs. The cross-task analysis qualifies steerability's applicability, while expanded positioning, clearer figures and a code pointer improve usability. These provide meaningful incremental validation and clarity gains without changing the main method, task coverage or original benchmark results.
